'''ZA/UM '''is an independent [[video game developer]] and publisher, and former cultural association, based in the United Kingdom. Originally a cultural collective founded in 2009, ZA/UM was registered as a company in 2015<ref>{{Cite web |title=ZA/UM |url=https://zaumstudio.com/zaumstudio.com/index |access-date=11 November 2026 |website=ZA/UM}}</ref> by novelists [[Robert Kurvitz]] and [[Kaur Kender]] in Estonia, and has offices in London and Brighton.

{{Nowrap|ZA/UM}}'s first game, ''[[Disco Elysium]]'', was released for Windows in October 2019 and macOS in April 2020. An expanded version of the game featuring full voice acting and new content, titled ''The Final Cut'', was released for consoles in 2021, alongside a free update for the PC versions. '''ZA/UM Atelier '''was launched in March 2021, featuring limited edition clothing and artwork inspired by concepts from the game.

Following the release of ''Disco Elysium'', several key contributors to {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}}, including founders Kurvitz and Kender left the organisation in acrimony, resulting in legal disputes. Several games the studio had in development were then cancelled, and 25% of the workforce laid off. In 2026, the studio's second game, ''[[Zero Parades: For Dead Spies]]'', was released. Although critically well-received, it sold poorly, resulting in a further round of layoffs.

==Background as a cultural association==
[[File:Robert Kurvitz.png|thumb|Founder, novelist [[Robert Kurvitz]] pictured in 2014]]
===Formation===
The core of what would become the ZA/UM collective was a group of high-school dropouts who called themselves The Overcoats in [[Tallinn]], Estonia. They would engage in long [[pen-and-paper role-playing game]] sessions that would form the basis of the world of ''Disco Elysium''.<ref name=":1">{{Cite book |last=ZA/UM|url=http://archive.org/details/discoelysiumartbook|title=Disco Elysium Digital Artbook|publisher=iam8bit|pages=}}</ref><ref name="gamesradar conception" /> The group also wrote provocative prose on a blog they called {{ill|NIHILIST.FM|et}}, which proved to be popular.<ref name="NYT">{{cite web|title=A Group of Socialists Created a Hit Game That Tore Them Apart|url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2025/09/17/arts/disco-elysium-zaum-estonia.html|date=17 September 2025|access-date=14 June 2026|author=Faber, Tom|website=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref>

In 2005, Kurvitz was playing in a band called Ultramelanhool and conceived of a fictional world during a drunken evening while listening to [[Tiësto]]'s "[[Adagio for Strings (Tiësto song)|Adagio for Strings]]".<ref name="gamesradar conception">{{Cite web |last=Wiltshire |first=Alex |date=9 January 2020 |title=The making of Disco Elysium: How {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}} created one of the most original RPGs of the decade |url=https://www.gamesradar.com/the-making-of-disco-elysium-how-zaum-created-one-of-the-most-original-rpgs-of-the-decade/ |access-date=8 April 2020 |website=[[GamesRadar]] |archive-date=9 January 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200109193447/https://www.gamesradar.com/the-making-of-disco-elysium-how-zaum-created-one-of-the-most-original-rpgs-of-the-decade/ |url-status=live}}</ref> The group then created a collective of artists and musicians called {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}} in 2009. The group was founded by [[Robert Kurvitz]], Martin Luiga, Jüri Saks, Aleksander Rostov and Joanna Ellmann.<ref name="NYT" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Luiga |first=Martin |date=2022-02-05 |title=HELLO FELLOW WORLDBUILDERS |url=https://medium.com/@martinluiga/hello-fellow-worldbuilders-6a3779a65d47 |access-date=2026-11-11 |website=Medium |language=en}}</ref> The name "za um", is a reference to the [[Zaum]] [[constructed language]] created by Russian avant-garde poets in the early 1900s. Its name can be read in Russian as a shortcut for the idiom {{lang|ru|взяться за ум}} ({{transliteration|ru|vzyat'sya za um}}), which is similar to the English idea of [[bootstrapping]]. The use of [[Letter case|all-capitals]] and the [[Slash (punctuation)|slash symbol]] is to present the team as "something that definitely exists and weighs eight tonnes".<ref name="gamesradar conception" />

===''Sacred and Terrible Air'' and Kurvitz-Kender relationship===
During this period, Kurvitz met Estonian author [[Kaur Kender]], who helped him to write a novel set in this world, ''Sacred and Terrible Air'',<ref name="Kurvitz">{{Cite web |last=Macgregor |first=Jody |date=2 November 2019 |title=Disco Elysium's lead designer wants to make an expansion and sequel, has already written a novel |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/disco-elysiums-lead-designer-wants-to-make-an-expansion-and-sequel-has-already-written-a-novel/ |access-date=13 November 2019 |website=[[PC Gamer]] |archive-date=4 November 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191104094551/https://www.pcgamer.com/disco-elysiums-lead-designer-wants-to-make-an-expansion-and-sequel-has-already-written-a-novel/ |url-status=live}}</ref> which was published in 2013 but only sold about one thousand copies. Kurvitz fell into a period of depression and alcoholism for about three years following the book's commercial failure.<ref name="gamesradar conception" /> The failure of ''Sacred and Terrible Air'', along with Kurvitz and Rostov's teenage experience with ''[[Dungeons and Dragons]],'' would inspire {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}}'s design philosophy of embracing failure.<ref name="zaum hungarian interview">{{Cite web |last=Metsniit |first=Mikk |date=31 March 2017 |title=The Hungarian Interview |url=https://zaumstudio.com/2017/03/31/the-hungarian-interview/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201202012348/https://zaumstudio.com/2017/03/31/the-hungarian-interview/ |archive-date=2 December 2020 |access-date=8 April 2020 |website={{Nowrap|ZA/UM}} Studio}}</ref>

In 2013, Kender was made the acting editor-in-chief for the cultural newspaper ''[[Sirp]]'' after a failed contest to fill the role and a round of layoffs. Kender recruited Kurvitz as an editor for this endeavour, but the two were accused of copyright infringement for publishing an unpublished work by poet Andres Aule, and resigned on November 25.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lust|first=Katrin|date=25 November 2013|title=Kaur Kender ja Robert Kurvitz panid pillid kotti|url=https://elu24.postimees.ee/2608576/kaur-kender-ja-robert-kurvitz-panid-pillid-kotti|access-date=29 October 2023|website=Postimees|language=et}}</ref> The cultural minister [[Rein Lang]] also resigned for allegedly interfering with the magazine through his support for Kender.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lang sees no chance to continue|url=https://www.baltictimes.com/news/articles/33834/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260519035553/https://www.baltictimes.com/news/articles/33834/|archive-date=2026-05-19|access-date=2026-11-11|website=[[The Baltic Times]]|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Estonian culture minister resigns over newspaper scandal |url=https://www.baltictimes.com/news/articles/33904/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260517184739/https://www.baltictimes.com/news/articles/33904/ |archive-date=2026-05-17 |access-date=2026-11-11 |website=[[The Baltic Times]] |language=en}}</ref> Kurvitz would later describe his experience with the national cultural magazine as a "clownish disaster" that turned the group from being "completely ignored" to being the "dark joke of the year".<ref name=":12">{{Cite book |last=ZA/UM|url=http://archive.org/details/discoelysiumartbook|title=Disco Elysium Digital Artbook|publisher=iam8bit|pages=}}</ref>

Kurvitz eventually managed to overcome his alcoholism and helped Kender in his own recovery. As a sign of gratitude, Kender suggested to Kurvitz that instead of pursuing a novel, he could try capturing his world as a video game to draw a larger interest. Kurvitz had no experience in video games, but once he saw the artwork of the game's setting easily fitting into an [[isometric RPG|isometric format]], as well as Rostov's agreement that they might as well continue taking the risk of failing on a video game together, Kurvitz proceeded with the idea. They registered {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}} as a company in 2015 to develop the game.<ref name="gamesradar conception" />

==''Disco Elysium''==
===Development and move of {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}} to the UK=== 
Work on ''Disco Elysium'' started around 2016, with the local team living in a [[Squatting|squat]] in a former gallery in Tallinn. They were able to secure venture capital into the game during the first year, which allowed Kurvitz to seek out the English band [[Sea Power|British Sea Power]] for music for [[Disco Elysium (soundtrack)|the game's soundtrack]]. While in [[Birmingham]] to speak to the band, Kurvitz realised England was a better location for the main development team as there were more local resources for both development and for voice-overs.<ref name="gamesradar conception" /> During development, some of the staff relocated from Estonia to London and [[Brighton]], with other designers working out of Poland, Romania, and China.<ref name=gamesindustry.biz /><ref name="Postimees">{{Cite news |last=Altküla |first=Magnus |date=22 October 2019 |title=Kaur Kender on new computer game: It's like 'Truth and Justice' |work=[[Postimees]] |url=https://news.postimees.ee/6807443/kaur-kender-on-new-computer-game-it-s-like-truth-and-justice |access-date=29 December 2019 |archive-date=9 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211109102440/https://news.postimees.ee/6807443/kaur-kender-on-new-computer-game-it-s-like-truth-and-justice |url-status=live}}</ref> Overall, by the time of the game's release, {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}} had about 20 outside consultants and 35 in-house developers,<ref name="gamesradar conception" /> with a team of eight writers assisting Kurvitz in the game's dialogue.<ref name="gamesindustry.biz">{{Cite web |last=Batchelor |first=James |date=21 July 2017 |title=Making games under threat of nuclear war |url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/articles/2017-07-20-making-games-under-threat-of-nuclear-war |website=[[GamesIndustry.biz]] |access-date=15 October 2019 |archive-date=21 July 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170721133420/https://www.gamesindustry.biz/articles/2017-07-20-making-games-under-threat-of-nuclear-war |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Price |first=Edward |date=20 April 2018 |title=Disco Elysium – Rezzed 2018 Interview |url=https://gameanalytics.com/blog/disco-elysium-rezzed-2018-interview.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191019105734/https://gameanalytics.com/blog/disco-elysium-rezzed-2018-interview.html |archive-date=19 October 2019 |access-date=19 October 2019 |website=GameAnalytics}}</ref> The majority of the game's funding was provided by Estonian businessman Margus Linnamäe.<ref name=Postimees /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Helemäe |first=Deisi |date=5 September 2018 |title=Kaur Kenderi uus videomänguäri on neelanud juba 700 000 eurot investorite raha |trans-title=Kaur Kender's new video game business has already absorbed 700,000 euros of investors' money |url=https://raha.geenius.ee/rubriik/uudis/kaur-kenderi-uus-videomanguari-on-neelanud-juba-700-000-eurot-investorite-raha/ |access-date=30 December 2019 |website=Geenius.ee |language=et ===Expansion of scope and delay===
As originally planned, the game was to focus on action in a single city location to make the 2017 release. However, as {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}} had indicated to investors that this was to be a game that spanned a larger world, they found the need to spread beyond that single location, forcing them to delay the game's release, along with the name change to ''Disco Elysium''.<ref name="gamesradar conception" /> Kurvitz had always anticipated the ''No Truce'' title to be more of a working title and wanted to reserve it for when they had bundled ''Disco Elysium'' with a second planned game.<ref name="egm title">{{Cite magazine |last=O'Keefe |first=David |date=20 January 2020 |title=The Invisible Art of Game Titles |url=https://egmnow.com/the-invisible-art-of-game-titles/ |magazine=[[Electronic Gaming Monthly]] |access-date=8 April 2020 |archive-date=11 January 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200111172653/https://egmnow.com/the-invisible-art-of-game-titles/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Though {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}} had initially planned to publish the game through [[Humble Bundle]], they ultimately chose to self-publish it.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Tarason |first=Dominic |date=9 March 2018 |title=No Truce With The Furies gets a mad new title and trailer |work=[[Rock Paper Shotgun]] |url=https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/2018/03/09/no-truce-with-the-furies-gets-a-mad-new-title-and-trailer/ |access-date=16 October 2019 |archive-date=17 October 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191017031304/https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/2018/03/09/no-truce-with-the-furies-gets-a-mad-new-title-and-trailer/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

===Release and reception===
''Disco Elysium'' received universal critical acclaim upon its release,<ref name="PCGUS">{{Cite web |last=Kelly |first=Andy |date=15 October 2019 |title=Disco Elysium Review |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/disco-elysium-review/ |access-date=15 October 2019 |website=[[PC Gamer]] |archive-date=15 October 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191015195613/https://www.pcgamer.com/disco-elysium-review/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="MC">{{Cite web |title=Disco Elysium for PC Reviews |url=https://www.metacritic.com/game/disco-elysium/critic-reviews/?platform=pc |access-date=10 March 2020 |publisher=[[Metacritic]] |url-status=live}}</ref> winning numerous awards, notably at the [[The Game Awards 2019|Game Awards 2019]] (Best Independent Game, Best Narrative, Best Role Playing Game, Fresh [[Indie game|Indie Game]]).<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DOz4QcRZu_g |title=Disco Elysium Wins the Fresh Indie Game Award Presented by Reggie Fils-Aimé |date=2019-12-12 |last=thegameawards |access-date=2026-07-01 |via=YouTube}}</ref> It sold more than five million copies,<ref name="nytimes2025">{{cite web |last1=Faber |first1=Tom |title=A Group of Socialists Created a Hit Game That Tore Them Apart |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2025/09/17/arts/disco-elysium-zaum-estonia.html |website=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=19 September 2025 |date=17 September 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251004014110/https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2025/09/17/arts/disco-elysium-zaum-estonia.html|archive-date=4 October 2025|url-status=live}}</ref> and is regarded by some critics as one of the [[greatest video games of all time]],<ref>{{Cite web |author=Slant Staff |date=2020-04-13 |title=The 100 Best Video Games of All Time |url=https://www.slantmagazine.com/games/the-100-best-video-games-of-all-time/ |access-date=2025-04-08 |website=[[Slant Magazine]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |author=I. G. N. Staff |date=2021-12-31 |title=The Top 100 Video Games of All Time |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/the-best-100-video-games-of-all-time |access-date=2025-04-08 |website=IGN |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Best Games on PC |url=https://www.metacritic.com/browse/game/pc/ |access-date=2025-04-08 |website=[[Metacritic]] |language=en}}</ref> and a strong example of [[video games as an art form]].

== Breakup of ZA/UM ==
Following the critical and commercial success of ''Disco Elysium'', work immediately began on a direct sequel to the game as well as several spin-off projects.<ref name="PCGinterview">{{Cite web |last=Litchfield |first=Ted |date=2024-06-13 |title=A follow-up to the legendary Disco Elysium might have been ready to play within the next year⁠—{{Nowrap|ZA/UM}}'s devs loved it, management canceled it and laid off the team: 'For a while it seemed like miracles were possible, and with them redemption' |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/gaming-industry/game-development/for-a-while-it-seemed-like-miracles-were-possible-and-with-them-redemption-a-follow-up-to-the-legendary-disco-elysium-might-have-been-ready-to-play-within-the-next-yearzaums-devs-loved-it-management-canceled-it-and-laid-off-the-team/ |access-date=2024-07-10 |website=PC Gamer}}</ref> The direct sequel, code-named Y12, was led by Kurvitz, Rostov, and Hindpere. Another project, P1, was led by Kender.<ref name="PCGinterview" />

===Departures of Kurvitz and key members===
In October 2022, {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}} member Martin Luiga announced that he, Kurvitz, Rostov, and Hindpere of {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}} had "involuntarily left the company" in late 2021, stating that {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}} "no longer represents the ethos it was founded on." Luiga also affirmed that the {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}} [[Cultural institution|cultural association]] had also been dissolved.<ref name="pcgamer departures">{{Cite web |last=Litchfield |first=Ted |date=1 October 2022 |title=Founding member of Disco Elysium developer claims core team members 'involuntarily' left the company |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/founding-member-of-disco-elysium-developer-claims-core-team-members-involuntarily-left-the-company/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221001200459/https://www.pcgamer.com/founding-member-of-disco-elysium-developer-claims-core-team-members-involuntarily-left-the-company/ |archive-date=1 October 2022 |access-date=1 October 2022 |website=[[PC Gamer]]}}</ref> In an interview, Luiga stated that the other three members had been fired under [[false pretenses]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Laska |first=Karol |date=6 October 2022 |title='Fans Have the Right to Know' - Disco Elysium Co-Creator Talks {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}} Losing With the System |url=https://www.gamepressure.com/newsroom/fans-have-the-right-to-know-disco-elysium-co-creator-talks-zaum-l/z04ad7 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221006143921/https://www.gamepressure.com/newsroom/fans-have-the-right-to-know-disco-elysium-co-creator-talks-zaum-l/z04ad7 |archive-date=6 October 2022 |access-date=6 October 2022 |website=Gamepressure.com |language=en}}</ref> A spokesperson for {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}} denied the allegations.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Batchelor |first=James |date=3 October 2022 |title=Three key members of Disco Elysium studio have left 'involuntarily' |url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/three-key-members-of-disco-elysium-studio-have-left-involuntarily |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221003112200/https://www.gamesindustry.biz/three-key-members-of-disco-elysium-studio-have-left-involuntarily |archive-date=3 October 2022 |magazine=[[Game Informer]] |access-date=8 October 2022}}</ref>

In early November 2022, conflicting reports of the events were announced. According to Kurvitz, Zaum Studio OÜ, the development studio, was originally owned in majority shares by Margus Linnamäe, and was then acquired by Tütreke OÜ, a holding company owned by studio CEO Ilmar Kompus through a share purchase in 2021. Kurvitz and Rostov claimed that the funds used for that purchase were pulled from the studio itself, making it a fraudulent purchase, upon which they started to challenge the purchase and recover their IP from the studio.<ref name="gr nov2022" /> Among Kurvitz' and Rostov's complaints is that Kompus purchased four sketches from {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}} that were establishing the basis for a ''Disco Elysium'' sequel for {{GBP|1}}, then resold these to Zaum for {{Euro|4.8 million}}, effectively helping Kompus regain part of the money spent to acquire {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}} through Tütreke.

Kurvitz and Rostov discovered the change in how the company was organised, including their demotion, and were fired when they began raising questions. Kurvitz and Rostov argued that they still have some control of the ''Disco Elysium'' [[intellectual property]] rights, and thus should have had a say in blocking the sale.<ref name="gr nov2022">{{Cite web |last=Bailey |first=Dustin |date=November 9, 2022 |title=Fired Disco Elysium devs allege fraud, while the studio alleges toxic management |url=https://www.gamesradar.com/fired-disco-elysium-devs-allege-fraud-while-the-studio-alleges-toxic-management/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221109223130/https://www.gamesradar.com/fired-disco-elysium-devs-allege-fraud-while-the-studio-alleges-toxic-management/ |archive-date=9 November 2022 |access-date=November 9, 2022 |website=[[GamesRadar]]}}</ref><ref name="pcgamer legal update">{{Cite web |last=Straton |first=Rich |date=November 22, 2022 |title=The legal war over Disco Elysium reaches Disco Elysium levels of complexity |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/the-legal-war-over-disco-elysium-reaches-disco-elysium-levels-of-complexity/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221122191538/https://www.pcgamer.com/the-legal-war-over-disco-elysium-reaches-disco-elysium-levels-of-complexity/ |archive-date=22 November 2022 |access-date=November 24, 2022 |website=[[PC Gamer]]}}</ref> {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}} denied the charges in a statement, and alleged that the former employees had been let go for creating a disruptive environment at the studio, claiming that the two had "limited to no engagement in their responsibility and work", as well as verbally abused and discriminated against other employees.<ref name="pcgamer legal update" /> Other employees of {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}}, speaking anonymously with ''[[GamesIndustry.biz]]'', claimed the situation was "not black and white".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Partis |first=Danielle |date=November 9, 2022 |title=Disco Elysium studio {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}} confirms former employees were fired for misconduct |url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/disco-elysium-studio-zaum-confirms-former-employees-were-fired-for-misconduct |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221109164302/https://www.gamesindustry.biz/disco-elysium-studio-zaum-confirms-former-employees-were-fired-for-misconduct |archive-date=9 November 2022 |access-date=November 9, 2022 |website=[[GamesIndustry.biz]]}}</ref>

===Legal disputes===
Legal proceedings in the matter were started by Kaur Kender, the executive producer of ''Disco Elysium''. Kender had asked similar questions of the change in {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}}'s management, leading to his firing.<ref name="pcgamer legal update" /> He filed suit asserting that Kompus owed him {{Euro|1 million}}. Kender further asserted that Kompus was aided by Tõnis Haavel, an Estonian investor and Kompus' brother-in-law<ref name="SITuulik">{{Cite web |last=Wutz |first=Marco |date=2024-02-16 |title=Last Disco Elysium writer laid off by {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}} speaks out |url=https://videogames.si.com/news/disco-elysium-dev-zaum-layoffs-last-writer-speaks-out |access-date=2024-07-10 |website=GLHF}}</ref> who had been convicted of fraud and was already {{Euro|11.5 million}} in debt.<ref name="pcgamer legal update" /> Haavel has a majority share in Yessirnosir Ltd., a United Kingdom subsidiary of {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}} where the ''Disco Elysium'' rights are held. An initial hearing in Kender's case, which included statements from Kurvitz, was held in October 2022.<ref name="pcgamer legal update" /> By December 2022, Kender had dropped his lawsuit, as Kompus had paid back {{Euro|4.8 million}} from Tütreke back to {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}}.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Partis |first=Danielle |date=December 8, 2022 |title=Lawsuit against {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}} majority shareholder withdrawn |url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/lawsuit-against-zaum-majority-shareholder-withdrawn |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221208142756/https://www.gamesindustry.biz/lawsuit-against-zaum-majority-shareholder-withdrawn |archive-date=8 December 2022 |access-date=December 8, 2022 |website=[[GamesIndustry.biz]]}}</ref><ref name="pcgamer dec2022">{{Cite web |last=Litchfield |first=Ted |date=December 10, 2022 |title=$4.8 million paid to {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}} and one lawsuit dropped as the battle over Disco Elysium continues |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/dollar48-million-paid-to-zaum-and-one-lawsuit-dropped-as-the-battle-over-disco-elysium-continues/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221210200805/https://www.pcgamer.com/dollar48-million-paid-to-zaum-and-one-lawsuit-dropped-as-the-battle-over-disco-elysium-continues/ |archive-date=10 December 2022 |access-date=December 10, 2022 |website=[[PC Gamer]]}}</ref> Kurvitz and Rostov still assert that there were illegal actions to take over the development studio leading to their ouster.<ref name="pcgamer dec2022" />

The studio issued a statement on 14 March 2023 stating that all legal actions from the former members were concluded. Of Kender, he had "divested all his shares in the studio, repaid all his debts to the studio", and paid for the studio's legal fees under court order. Of Kurvitz and Rostov, the studio alleged that their lawsuit was dropped due to a lack of evidence. Further details of these cases remain confidential.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wales |first=Matt |date=March 14, 2023 |title=Disco Elysium studio says lawsuits from former members have been resolved |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/disco-elysium-studio-says-lawsuits-from-former-members-have-been-resolved |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230314232339/https://www.eurogamer.net/disco-elysium-studio-says-lawsuits-from-former-members-have-been-resolved |archive-date=14 March 2023 |access-date=March 14, 2023 |website=[[Eurogamer]]}}</ref> On 17 March 2023, Kurvitz and Rostov responded to this statement by clarifying that the announcement was "wrong and misleading in several respects" and "[sought] to unfairly paint [them] - the remaining minority shareholders in {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}} - as mere disgruntled employees." Kurvitz and Rostov also stated that their lawsuit regarding employment claims against the studio was dismissed "as part of a larger campaign against [them]" and that they plan to "pursue legal options accordingly."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Litchfield |first=Ted |date=March 18, 2023 |title=Disco Elysium studio declares 'resolution' of legal battle while two of its ousted founders insist the fight continues: 'they will not silence us' |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/disco-elysium-studio-declares-resolution-of-legal-battle-while-two-of-its-ousted-founders-insist-the-fight-continues-they-will-not-silence-us/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230320022925/https://www.pcgamer.com/disco-elysium-studio-declares-resolution-of-legal-battle-while-two-of-its-ousted-founders-insist-the-fight-continues-they-will-not-silence-us/ |archive-date=20 March 2023 |access-date=March 19, 2023 |website=[[PC Gamer]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rousseau |first=Jeffrey |date=2023-03-14 |title={{Nowrap|ZA/UM}} resolves legal dispute with Disco Elysium producer Kaur Kender |url=https://www.gamesindustry.biz/zaum-resolves-legal-dispute-with-disco-elysium-producer-kaur-kender |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230321211432/https://www.gamesindustry.biz/zaum-resolves-legal-dispute-with-disco-elysium-producer-kaur-kender |archive-date=21 March 2023 |access-date=2023-03-21 |website=[[GamesIndustry.biz]] |language=en}}</ref> In May 2023, [[People Make Games]] published the findings of their investigation into {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}}'s legal situation, in which Tuulik was featured heavily in interviews.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Litchfield |first=Ted |date=2023-06-02 |title=After watching the explosive documentary on Disco Elysium's legal battle, I can't fathom how Disco Elysium 2 will ever be made |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/after-watching-the-explosive-documentary-on-disco-elysiums-legal-battle-i-cant-fathom-how-disco-elysium-2-will-ever-be-made/ |access-date=2024-07-10 |website=PC Gamer}}</ref> Klindžić alleged that company executives isolated Tuulik in retaliation for unfavorable comments made toward them in the documentary.   

=== Abortive projects ===
Following the ouster of Kurvitz, Rostov, and Hindpere, work on the direct sequel project Y12 continued for several months under Argo Tuulik, one of the writers on ''Disco Elysium'', and Dora Klindžić until management cancelled it in mid-2022.<ref name="PCGinterview" /> Shortly thereafter, Tuulik and Klindžić were asked to pitch a "standalone expansion" to ''Disco Elysium'', X7, later revealed to be titled ''Locust City: A Disco Elysium Story'', which centered on the characters of Cuno and Cunoesse.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Egan |first=Toussaint |date=2025-04-02 |title=A would-be Disco Elysium expansion has leaked online, with lots of details |url=https://www.polygon.com/gaming/551096/disco-elysium-locust-city-an-elysium-story-zaum-presentation |access-date=2025-04-07 |website=Polygon |language=en-US}}</ref> The game was greenlighted by management without a [[pre-production]] period. Full production began before the understaffed writing duo had a full outline of the game. They gained additional staff when Kender's project P1 was cancelled pursuant to his ouster.<ref name="PCGinterview" /> The team produced a "well-received" internal demo for X7 at the end of 2023.<ref name="PCGinterview" />   

In February 2024, ''[[Sports Illustrated]]''{{'}}s gaming publication ''GLHF'' reported that {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}} was laying off about 25% of its staff, including Tuulik and Klindžić, cancelling X7, and confirmed the earlier cancellation of Y12.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wutz |first=Marco |date=2024-02-15 |title=Sources: Disco Elysium dev {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}} to lay off around a quarter of its staff, cancels new game |url=https://videogames.si.com/news/disco-elysium-dev-zaum-layoffs |access-date=2024-07-10 |website=GLHF}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Wales |first=Matt |date=2024-02-15 |title=Disco Elysium standalone expansion reportedly cancelled and quarter of staff facing redundancy at {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}} |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/disco-elysium-standalone-expansion-reportedly-cancelled-and-quarter-of-staff-facing-redundancy-at-zaum |access-date=2024-07-10 |work=Eurogamer.net}}</ref> Tuulik noted that the layoffs primarily targeted women and team members who had raised complaints about working conditions.<ref name="SITuulik" /> ''[[PC Gamer]]'' reported that the only remaining projects at {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}} were M0, a ''Disco Elysium'' [[mobile game]], and C4, an unrelated RPG.<ref name="PCGinterview" /> In March 2025, ZA/UM revealed C4 as ''Zero Parades'', not connected in story or setting with ''Disco Elysium'', nor considered as a [[spiritual successor]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.polygon.com/gaming/537711/zaum-game-teaser-trailer-not-disco-elysium-2/ |title=ZA/UM announces its mysterious, highly anticipated follow-up to Disco Elysium |first=Toussaint |last=Egan |date=11 March 2025 |accessdate=28 March 2026 |work=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/games/rpg/we-finally-saw-za-ums-zero-parades-in-action-and-even-though-its-extremely-disco-elysium-the-protagonist-couldnt-be-more-different/ |title=We finally saw ZA/UM's Zero Parades in action and even though it's extremely Disco Elysium, the protagonist couldn't be more different |first=Tyler |last=  Colp |date=24 September 2025 |accessdate=28 September 2025 |work=[[PC Gamer]]}}</ref>

=== Splinter studios ===
The conflicts around the {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}} studio and breakup of the team led to four different projects from different members each seeking to be a successor to ''Disco Elysium'', in addition to ZA/UM's own ''Zero Parades''.<ref name="NYT" /> After leaving {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}}, Kurvitz and Rostov launched Red Info in June 2022, a development studio to work on a [[spiritual successor]] to ''Disco Elysium''.<ref>{{cite web |last=Litchfield |first=Ted |date=June 2, 2023 |title=After watching the explosive documentary on Disco Elysium's legal battle, I can't fathom how Disco Elysium 2 will ever be made |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/after-watching-the-explosive-documentary-on-disco-elysiums-legal-battle-i-cant-fathom-how-disco-elysium-2-will-ever-be-made/ |accessdate=October 11, 2024 |work=[[PC Gamer]]}}</ref> Red Info has been backed by at least $10 million in funding by [[NetEase]] and has brought writer [[Chris Avellone]] to help.<ref name="NYT" />

Three other spiritual successor projects were announced nearly simultaneously in October 2024 by three separate studios, each with some former members of {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}}.

* Longdue includes Martin Luiga—formerly of Red Info<ref>{{cite web |last=Warren |first=Mark |date=March 11, 2025 |title=Hopetown's latest ex-Disco Elysium recruit reveals he's had to leave another of the kinda Disco Elysium successor studios, but says it's on friendly terms |url=https://www.vg247.com/hopetown-latest-ex-disco-elysium-recruit-reveals-hes-left-another-would-be-successor-studio |access-date=April 24, 2025 |work=[[VG 247]]}}</ref>—plus ''Disco Elysium'' narrator Lenval Brown<ref>{{cite web |last=Nightingale |first=Ed |date=March 11, 2025 |title=More Disco Elysium alumni join former staff at Longdue working on spiritual successor |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/more-disco-elysium-alumni-join-former-staff-at-longdue-working-on-spiritual-successor |access-date=April 24, 2025 |work=[[Eurogamer]]}}</ref> and other developers from [[Bungie]] and [[Rockstar Games]]. Longdue announced their game [[Hopetown (video game)|Hopetown]] was funded via a [[Kickstarter]] campaign in April 2025.<ref>{{cite web |last=Reuben |first=Nic |date=October 11, 2024 |title=Former Disco Elysium devs are working on a spiritual successor at new studio Longdue, though Robert Kurvitz and Aleksander Rostov aren't involved |url=https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/former-disco-elysium-devs-are-working-on-a-spiritual-successor-at-new-studio-longdue-though-robert-kurvitz-and-aleksander-rostov-arent-involved |access-date=October 11, 2024 |work=[[Rock Paper Shotgun]]}}</ref>
* Dark Math Games was founded by investor Linnamae, and includes Kender and other {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}} developers. Dark Math is developing ''Tangerine Antarctic'' (previously named ''XXX Nightshift'').<ref>{{cite web |last=Wolans |first=Joshua |date=October 11, 2024 |title=A Disco Elysium successor studio has been announced for the second time today, meaning there are now 4 companies battling for the title of {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}}'s true inheritor |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/games/rpg/a-disco-elysium-successor-studio-has-been-announced-for-the-second-time-today-meaning-there-are-now-4-companies-battling-for-the-title-of-za-ums-true-inheritor/ |accessdate=October 11, 2024 |work=[[PC Gamer]]}}</ref><ref name="NYT" /> 
* [[Summer Eternal]] was founded by writers Argo Tuulik and Dora Klindžić. Both had worked previously with Dark Math and Longdue, but left these studios due to internal conflicts.<ref name="NYT" /><ref>{{cite web |last=Yin-Poole |first=Wesley |date=November 19, 2024 |title=The Wild Story Behind Disco Elysium's Spiritual Successors: Allegations, Legal Threats, and a USB Stick |url=https://za.ign.com/disco-elysium-1/203482/news/the-wild-story-behind-disco-elysiums-spiritual-successors-allegations-legal-threats-and-a-usb-stick |access-date=April 24, 2025 |work=[[IGN]]}}</ref> Summer Eternal later brought on Olga Moskvina and other senior developers from {{Nowrap|ZA/UM}}.<ref>{{cite web |last=Evans-Thirlwell |first=Edwin |date=October 11, 2024 |title=Sure, why not – third group of former Disco Elysium devs announce "revolutionary new RPG studio" |url=https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/sure-why-not-third-group-of-former-disco-elysium-devs-announce-revolutionary-new-rpg-studio |accessdate=October 11, 2024 |work=[[Rock Paper Shotgun]]}}</ref> In October 2026, they announced their Disco-like game in making – [[Red Rooster (video game)|''Red Rooster'']].

==''Zero Parades''==
In 2026, the studio's second game, ''[[Zero Parades: For Dead Spies]]'', was released on Windows and Playstation 5. Like ''Disco Elysium'', it was a single-player role playing game in isometric view. It was set in a new universe of Portofiro, with communist, neoliberal and fascist factions. Writers Siim "Kosmos" Sinamäe and [[Honey Watson]] said that unlike ''Disco Elysium'' which was a cop story, ''Zero Parades'' is a spy story, where there is necessarily no right or wrong action, making the game more suitable to the systems they had developed for it. ''Zero Parades'' was inspired primarily by the spy novels of [[John le Carré]], which Watson said were more intellectual compared to [[James Bond]], and about a person doing "sneaky, horrible things" as part of their espionage, and allows the player to opt to role-play more directly with Hershel.<ref name="polygon inspiration">{{cite web |url=https://www.polygon.com/zero-parades-interview-disco-elysium-zaum/ |title=The Disco Elysium team brushes off expectations for all new original game: 'Pressure is a privilege' |first=Giovanni |last=Colantonio |date=12 March 2026 |accessdate=28 March 2026 |work=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]}}</ref> Additionally, the works of [[Ursula K. Le Guin]] and [[Thomas Pynchon]] inspired the story.<ref name="polygon inspiration" />

It was critically well-received,<ref name="MCPCZP">{{cite web|title=Zero Parades: For Dead Spies — PC Critic Reviews|url=https://www.metacritic.com/game/zero-parades-for-dead-spies/critic-reviews/?platform=pc|website=[[Metacritic]]|access-date=June 8, 2026}}</ref><ref name="ZP">{{cite web|title=ZERO PARADES: For Dead Spies Reviews|url=https://opencritic.com/game/20490/zero-parades-for-dead-spies|website=[[OpenCritic]]|access-date=July 6, 2026}}</ref> attracting praise for its writing, and criticism for being derivative of ''Disco Elysium''.<ref name="GSpotR">{{Cite web |last=Wakeling |first=Richard |date=2026-05-18 |title=Zero Parades: For Dead Spies Review - Cascading Choices |url=https://www.gamespot.com/reviews/zero-parades-for-dead-spies-review-cascading-choices/1900-6418491/ |access-date=2026-05-23 |website=[[GameSpot]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bueno |first=Daniel |date=2026-05-21 |title=Review: Zero Parades Understands the Assignment |url=https://www.siliconera.com/review-zero-parades-understands-the-assignment/ |access-date=2026-05-23 |website=Siliconera |language=en-US}}</ref> The game's sales were below expectations, however, and in July 2026, ZA/UM announced a round of layoffs and redundancies, with 32 staff from across the studio released.<ref name="layoffs">{{Cite web |last=Rowe|first=Willa|date=2026-07-17 |title=Disco Elysium studio announces layoffs after new game flounders |url=https://www.polygon.com/disco-elysium-studio-za-um-layoffs/ |access-date=2026-07-17|website=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]] |language=en-US}}</ref>
